transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, what brings me in is that I keep getting hit out of nowhere with the scene of my cousin on that pavement. It's... it's like I can actually hear the shouting and see the flashing lights all over again. It just happens randomly, even when I'm just standing in the church office trying to do my job and act normal. It's getting to be too much to handle on my own.
Did you witness your cousin being seriously injured or killed?
Yes. He was... he was killed. I was right there when it happened.
When these episodes hit, does it feel as if you are back at the scene and it’s happening again right then?

Yeah, exactly. Like I mentioned a minute ago, it really does. It's not just remembering it. When it hits me out of nowhere—even if I'm just standing there in the church office—I'm right back on that pavement. I hear the exact same shouting, I see those flashing lights... it feels like it's happening right in front of me all over again.
How long ago did your cousin’s death happen?
It was... two years and three months ago. And this has all been going on ever since he was killed.
Do you go out of your way to avoid reminders of your cousin’s death?

Yeah, I do. I actually take the long way around town now just so I don't have to pass the community center or that court. And if... if somebody starts talking about that night, I just shut it down, or I find an excuse to leave the room. I just can't be around it.
Since your cousin died, have you been constantly on guard or easily startled?

Yeah, definitely. I'm always on edge now. Like... I can't even sit with my back to a door anymore. And when I'm at church events, instead of paying attention to the people right in front of me, I'm just constantly scanning. I'm always watching people's hands, checking the corners, or noticing if a car is slowing down outside. I just always have to know exactly where the nearest exit is.
